My overall take is it's a fun game you'll get plenty of time out of if you end up enjoying the gameplay loop. That said, as someone who played the previous title from the 3DS there are two different perspectives: Someone new or someone who has played the original Fantasy Life.

---

So starting from a fresh perspective:

Fantasy Life is an action RPG where you play one of several "Lives", or jobs. Combat jobs, crafting jobs, and gathering jobs. Your objective in the game is a loop of progressing the story to open up more of the world to enable seeing more new stuff and advancing your Lives to access more content.

Put more simply, the game's very progression oriented. Aside from wanting to see new locations and characters your main motivation is to progress the ranks of these jobs, as they require you to do things like defeat certain new monsters or craft a certain array of new tools or

First off, my playtime for this game is grossly inaccurate due to playing this on a Rog Ally and leaving it in hibernate for too long...whoops.  My accurate playtime is around 110 hours.

This is my GOTY for 2025.  I did play the original Fantasy Life shortly after release on the DS, in Japanese, and had mostly forgotten it by the time this sequel came out.  Some references went over my head but overall, knowledge of the first game is not required at all.  

Some of the statements about this being a cozy game feel really off to me.  The marketing stating that it's a "slow-life JRPG", I would agree with to some extent, however.  Calling this a cozy game really does it a disservice, as this really plays more like a Japanese MMO, with the content and longevity to back that up.  It deserves to be at a AAA JRPG price point, and not a "cozy game" lower price point like something in the vein of

The title lives up to its name cause this game really STOLE MY TIME!

Fantasy life vet and 40 year old virgin here: It's better than ever.

It’s like Breath of the Wild and Animal Crossing smashed together.

The fact that this game had more content on day one than Animal Crossing has had in over five years is amazing. I love it so much that I bought it for Steam and Switch. And as soon as my wife’s boyfriend stops making love to my wife I will buy him a copy too. Fantasy Life on the 3DS was an underrated masterpiece, and I'm so glad it's now getting the attention it deserves! So much depth of gameplay, and so much replay value. It's refreshing to have a game fully fleshed out at launch. The story is delightfully silly and doesn't take itself too seriously. 

I gotta say though it’s so bizarre seeing Fantasy Life become this big popular thing in recent years, I'm so happy l could cry. The

I do recommend this game. So far in my journey I have unlocked each available "job" and raised them to fledgling level. It's an easy, sweet, "cozy" game. I love the characters and the play style. It brings to mind FF games and perhaps a style seeming much like Animal Crossing. The story seems sweet. I find it a delight. I have yet to play co-op with my son, but I know it will come. I think if you like a relaxed play style, farming, and crafting, you might enjoy this little game. I'm 71 and find it very easy to play. I also use a mouse and keyboard. Enjoy!

I put over 300 hours into the 3DS game and this one improves on that in just about every aspect. Aside from the usual Fantasy Life features, it adds a large open world side locale, a rogue-like dungeon and an Animal Crossing style island and islanders which add a lot of charm and fun to an already fantastic game. This is my 2025 GOTY for sure.
Animal Crossing New Horizons if it had gameplay and purpose

I don't think it's fair to review bomb Fantasy Life i just because LEVEL-5 is starting to use AI, especially since there is no evidence this specific game was developed using AI.

Fantasy Life i is a wonderful game with a lot of charm. The gameplay can be repetitive, but the variety keeps it fun. Just like in the original, you can be a knight one minute and a cook the next. There is a ton of fun to be had here. This entry in the fantasy Life serie also features a better story, and the "Legend" bosses can be genuinely challenging. I clocked 200 hours in the original and already have 113 hours in this one.

Regarding the AI slop issue:
I will be the first to denounce AI slop, and IF any future DLC turns into AI slop, I will 100% change my review. However, there is a responsible way to use AI. If it's used strictly for polish, it should be fine. In a 3D game, even individual blades of grass

Every moment was a wonderful experience.

Worth every penny.

[h1] Tough sell [/h1]

As a fervent admirer of the original Fantasy Life on the 3DS, I approached Fantasy Life i: The Girl Who Steals Time with sky-high expectations, hoping for a sequel that would expand on the vibrant, sprawling world of its predecessor. The original game was a triumph - a charming blend of exploration, character-driven storytelling, and a richly realized world brimming with unique locales and loveable NPCs. Unfortunately, Fantasy Life i feels like a hollow echo of that magic, a game that tries to do too much while forgetting what made its predecessor special. While it’s undeniably a good game with flashes of brilliance, it’s a deeply disappointing sequel that trades depth for gimmicks and nostalgia for fragmentation.

Let’s start with the positives: The combat system is a highlight, with fluid mechanics, a satisfying dodge system, and an engaging parry mechanic for th

Do you long for a streamlined version of Final Fantasy XIV's Combat/Gather/Craft gameplay?  Kill a rare mob to farm special leather to craft rare mining armor to farm a gem to make the designer bed of your dreams for your village.   An irresponsible amount of bars to fill, classes to level, recipes to learn, skill points to spend, and even more bars to fill.

A master-bar-tory dopamine rush of a good time.

[i]Potential trigger warning:  Twee Animal Crossing style presentation.
Potential selling point:  Twee Animal Crossing style presentation.[/i]

[h1] Fantasy Life i: The Game That Steals Time [/h1]

This game, as the aptly named title suggests, steals a ton of your time, and not all of it feels as though it was stolen in the name of fun. While the game is certainly cute, charming, robust, and highly entertaining, the grind may become an overwhelmingly negative factor that may or may not hamper your experience. If you enjoy a bit of a grind, this game can easily sink its claws into you for hundreds of hours. If you are annoyed by games that make you grind mindlessly for hours on end for meager amounts of EXP, then you may want to avoid this game.

[h3] Story: [/h3]

The story can be summarized fairly easily: Short and inconsequential. It's only a small part of the overall experience, and it is easily finished in 30 hours or less. It is a sweet tale of friendship and cooperation that spans the ages, a wholesome journey overall, but

NOTE: This review is for version 1.5.0 of the game.

Hello friends,

Today we will be reviewing the game Fantasy Life I: The Girl Who Steals Time. This is a continuation of the game made on the Nintendo 3ds. Having never played that version of the game, this review will only be talking specifically about this version of the game.

This is a life sim, similar to games like Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon. The difference that there are 14 life's, or jobs, a player can level up and use in the game. This makes leveling them all up to max a great endeavor that should only be done post game, after beating the full storyline. The storyline is a interesting time traveling twist where the character lives his life's in the past. Then use these to explore the present day. Be aware that some sections of the game require life's to be a specific level to continue the story, so it may require grinding o

Brings back memories of hiding my 3DS underneath my pillow when my parents came in to check if I'm sleeping. 
Very attached to the old game and probably would have preferred if we could've seen the familiar maps again etc, but that's just my bias. 

When it comes to the actual game though... it's good. But they had too many pots on the stove. Animal crossing island, open world botw, story, now a roguelike dlc... they just threw everything at the wall. It was a bit jarring at first to get introduced to one thing and then ripped out of it to be introduced to the next thing. All of it is decent, but none of it is fully done. The story feels... meh? Sure, the original wasn't a masterpiece either, but it really nailed its themes of friendship and unity. There was never a big bad, just people uniting their passions to save their world. Here it's just "this guy is evil because he can". Half of

It's just a really cute game to unwind for a few days. There isn't much of an endgame to speak of, aside from getting the most powerful gear and decorating your village.

It's disappointing that they haven't really supported the game after launch. All we got was a couple hotfixes, a photo mode, and a small DLC that introduces roguelike elements. This game could be so much more. They teased more updates months and months ago, but they haven't said anything.

This game would be perfect with more Animal Crossing elements, such as a museum, events, or holidays.

But aside from those small issues, the game is really nice.

So much to do in this game, it's crazy! If you want to kill some time and slowly build your character, you'll enjoy this. Constantly saying "one more thing" then bam, it's 2am. Reminds me of Darkcloud from the playstation days.

Lovely little grindy game where you level up 14 different Lives, each focused on its own task. Some Lives are definitely more fun than others, and the higher you get in a Life path, the grind becomes a lot more noticeable. The story is cute and charming, but nothing too special. Overall, it’s a cozy game that’s great if you enjoy progression and chill grinding.

Pretty similar to the one on DS (although not the same game).

If you don't like grinding, just forget this even exists, the "game" is all about that.
Combat and gathering are very basic, crafting is a mini-game, and you do all of that over and over with very little variation.

If that is not stopping you, then there is a decent amount of content, and unlike the previous game you can switch life on the fly (interract with a mining deposit and you switch to miner, click to attack and you switch to your last combat profession, go to a crafting table and you will switch based on the recipe you pick).
You can also change at any time from the menu.
This removes the most annoying part of the previous game.

I would have liked the skill trees to be more interesting and to unlock more interesting stuff rather than mostly stats.

however!! i do think this game is missing a lot of the heart and soul i enjoyed with the original fantasy life. like genuinely the original game was so full of life, and the map felt massive!! but in this game, despite there being more areas to explore, i think a lot of it is just missing that unique touch that would make it stand out. i think my biggest gripe is that all of the interior dungeons follow the same layout and look the same. i would understand it for the ra

I have very mixed feelings about this game. Yes it can be addicting, but it's also pretty lackluster. 

The game advertises itself with "14 unique jobs." When you see high playtime hours in steam reviews u might wrongly assume that it's due to the deep job system ❌ 
When the game opens up and you pick a job you get some quests, but those tutorial quests for each job will be the only ones you will get, after that you will get some generic tasks.

Regarding the classes themselves. The 4 combat ones are different enough. Meanwhile fishing/mining/cutting trees is just normal gathering available in most games but it's tied to levels, which just leads to grind. While the remaining lives are just crafting with the exact same mini game.

The main story is nothing groundbreaking, the characters aren't that memorable. It feels like the story just serves as a way to introduce the player to biomes,

Was it the nostalgia or was the original really that much better? After trying so desperately to fall in love with this game, overlooking what is quite possibly the worst camera ever put in any game period, or the dull and repetitive shade of green scattered everywhere like weeds in a garden, I realized that it wasn't the game I needed to love, it was myself.

The problem with freedom is that without direction, you're left shackled, forever to wander aimlessly in a world that's supposed to be so beautiful. [b]TLDR:[/b] The story and character writing are meh. The actual gameplay, however, is very fun and there’s a ton of different things to do. If you don't mind a lighthearted (forgettable) story but prioritize fun gameplay + variety, FLi is a good choice.

Also, it is flawless on a steam deck.
Probably my favorite 2025 release. Loads of content and a really fun game!

neg.text:
I bought this game specifically to play with my spouse, expecting a cozy, shared experience based on the store page and promotional videos.

While co-op technically exists, it takes several hours of solo play to unlock, and once available it is severely limited. Multiplayer sessions are time-restricted, with one player effectively treated as a temporary visitor rather than a full participant. This design does not evolve or improve later in the game.

These limitations are not clearly explained on the store page, and we would not have purchased the game had we known co-op was structured as short, time-limited visits instead of sustained shared play.

If you are buying this game primarily for multiplayer or to play with a partner, be aware that it does not offer a traditional or persistent co-op experience. Solo players may still enjoy it, but couples should proceed with caution.

This game was developed without AI at the time of release and Steam also did not mention the use of AI for this game and I hope it stays that way.

I can't list all the ways this game fails to live up to its predecessor, but here are a few:

The story and setting are uninspired and confusing. The previous game's very interesting world is nowhere to be seen, and the player must now jump between a half dozen strange little islands with little connection to one another and details from the first game haphazardly scattered around. The story involves a few recurring characters, but they too have lost their connection to the original Reveria. The new characters are fine, but the story can't be any better than its subpar setting.

Game mechanics are overall unfocused and shallow. Many "Quality of Life" features have been added, but they remove all sense of skill and pacing from the gameplay loop, turning it into a mindless grind. There are too many extra features and side adventures. I wish this game was trying to feel like Fantasy Life in

This ain't a "slow life RPG." It borrows that moniker from the first Fantasy Life but completely misses what that even means. Instead, you're a generic Zelda-style protag in a pretty mid plot about time travel, ancient evils, alternate timelines, chosen-one destinies, etc. And its constantly interrupting itself to introduce the next feature, cutscene, unlockable, collectable or mobile game mechanic, which it has a ton of.

It has some of the same charm, style and mechanics of the first game but its all been repurposed to create what's essentially the perfect endless mobile game experience. It might be charming enough to get you to come back in short bursts, but its too much. It never slows you down to just chill, take in the world, and actually role play the fantasy life. Everyone at the company that uses GenAI even slightly deserve to be run out of business, now and forever. Blacklist them.

Its not bad but it really does not feel right for me. I dunno, I feel like I've got a decent tolerance to the "anime" stuff in anime (you know what I mean) but this game is genuinely the first time I have played something and felt like im not in the target age demographic. I'm sure it gets less painful the further in you get, the start has a lot of story, but man, the story is not good and the character writing feels like a budget kids show. Every time someone speaks to me, I want to turn the game off. 
The gameplay and music are pretty nice but I just found the game so hard to want to return to.

As someone who fell in love with the original Fantasy Life on the 3DS, I was ecstatic when I learned that there was a sequel in the making. I was craving to pour in another 300+ hours into this game just like I did with the original game. As of writing this review, I am disheartened to say that I am disappointed with Fantasy Life i: The Girl Who Steals Time. The gameplay loop, the dungeon design, and the world itself... all of it greatly saddens me.

[Gameplay Loop]
To start off, I want to discuss the gameplay loop. Much like in the original, the game has you selecting various lives to pursue all the while making your way though the story. The design is still there, do thing, and progress. Nothing I would say is highly deviating from the 3DS version. The problem is the massive level of grinding you have do, and this is especially worse in the end game. I was so fed up with getting materi

100 hours in and now the game can no longer launch on the steam deck. I have attempted a ridiculous amount of "fixes" and workarounds with no joy.  It isn't worth this amount of effort and frustration.

This was an awful experience for co-op. My bf and I had to play over an hour just to get to the co op mode just to find out that it was not actually co op. It was a separate game and not apart of the main mission. You get only 30 minutes on an island just to explore and it has nothing to do with the main lore of the game for the co op mode. No missions like the individual game and wish I knew before wasting my boyfriend's money. If you want co op this game is not it. But if you are by yourself it has nice art.

I feel cheated out of my money.

Let it be known, I went into this game thinking it was a successor to the 3DS game, "Fantasy Life". The 3DS game still holds up as, dare I say, the best RPG on that system. This game is alright. I prefer the 3DS game, though.

Since then, Level5 claims to be "80 to 90% AI usage". I cannot support a company that uses AI for what should be human charm and creativity. I refuse to adjust my negative rating until they stop using AI.

While this game is fun, Level-5 has doubled down on their use of generative ai. I cannot refund this game as much as I would love to, but maybe adding a negative will give some people pause on if they should buy it.
No this game does not use generative ai. I hope it continues to not.
For games that used to have a great focus on their art, charm and quality. The use of generative ai is extremely offensive to their consumers. What's worse is the failure to disclose they have used generative ai in Inazuma eleven-Victory Road. If you need generative ai to make a game you shouldn't be making games anymore. I don't care if it's just for trailers or posters or background assets.
Generative ai has been implied by developers to be used heavily for all updates. Cannot recommend.
With the direction Level 5 is going, I strongly recommend just playing the first game instead.

Let me start by saying I really wanted to like this game.
Unfortunately that wasn't possible.

The outfits and character design are quite adorable.
The music is... fine, nothing ground-breaking, but also nothing jarring.

The life system as a whole is... pretty terrible. 14 lives you can freely change between sounds neat on paper, but the implementation is just... bad.
There's never a reason to change combat life, the game attempts to convince you that there are enemies that resist certain elements, but I can't

Guys save your Money, 

Since they only come up with absolutly AI Garbage you cant take it serious anymore ... sorry but this Game really aged like milk.

The previous game's very interesting world is nowhere to be seen, and the player must now jump between a half dozen strange little islands with little connection to one another and details from the first game haphazardly scattered around. The story involves a few recurring characters, but they too have lost their connection to the original Reveria. The new characters are fine, but the story can't be any better than its subpar setting.

Game mechanics are overall unfocused and shallow. Many "Quality of Life" features have been added, but they remove all sense of skill and pacing from the gameplay loop, turning it into a mindless grind. There are too many extra features and side adventures. I wish this game was trying to feel like Fantasy Life in

This ain't a "slow life RPG." It borrows that moniker from the first Fantasy Life but completely misses what that even means. Instead, you're a generic Zelda-style protag in a pretty mid plot about time travel, ancient evils, alternate timelines, chosen-one destinies, etc. And its constantly interrupting itself to introduce the next feature, cutscene, unlockable, collectable or mobile game mechanic, which it has a ton of.

It has some of the same charm, style and mechanics of the first game but its all been repurposed to create what's essentially the perfect endless mobile game experience. It might be charming enough to get you to come back in short bursts, but its too much. It never slows you down to just chill, take in the world, and actually role play the fantasy life. reviews.title: Animal Crossing if it was fun
reviews.text: I was skeptical at first because the App Store page didn't reflect the game very well. I'm glad I gave it a shot because it has genuinely rewarding and satisfying RNG + PvE elements plus much more content than I had initially anticipated. It has many mechanics similar to Animal Crossing but goes way farther in depth in a much more interactive experience. There's crafting, a bunch of different skills (lives) to level up with their own unlocks, you get your own island to build and decorate, and there's tons of different monsters (including bosses) that all have different drop tables that include rare items and gear. I am not exaggerating when I say this game is absolutely filled with content. The price is definitely worth it for this PC/ console game that runs surprisingly well on an IPhone.

reviews.title: Amazing port of Fantasy Life i: The Girl Who Steals Time
reviews.text:
This is a straight port of game that released last year on pc and consoles, at a fraction of the price! Anyone interested in this game just needs to search and read/watch reviews - there are plenty. In short- the game is part Rune Factory, Animal Crossing, and RuneScape with a sprinkle of Zelda. 

The touchscreen controls work very well in my opinion and it’s a perfect game to play for both short and long bursts. It’s a great fit for phones and having the ability to play this game truly anywhere on the fly is great!

It also has cross saves and cross play with the pc and console versions. The price of $25 may be steep for the mobile market, but you’re getting a full game that has all the same content as its $60 base game counterpart on pc and consoles. This is a steal!

reviews.text: I fell in love with the original Fantasy Life on 3DS over a decade ago. I’ve never found a game that quite scratches that itch and would always return to play it again. The best part is the game is fully cross save and cross play—I have my same save on Steam, Xbox, iOS, and Android.
